name: stri_split_regex
title: Split a String By Pattern Matches

origin.description: Split each string where a regular expression matches.
origin.usage: stri_split_regex(str, pattern, n = -1, omit_empty = FALSE, tokens_only = FALSE, simplify = FALSE, ..., opts_regex = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Character vector of regular expressions. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Maximum number of pieces. Negative means every piece. A value at least 2147483646 is an error.

arguments.name: omit_empty
arguments.text: TRUE drops empty pieces. NA replaces them with NA. FALSE keeps them.

arguments.name: tokens_only
arguments.text: If TRUE, a positive n keeps at most n whole pieces and drops the remainder.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: FALSE returns a list. TRUE pads a character matrix with empty strings. NA pads with NA.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: A list of regex settings, or NULL for the defaults.

origin.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. A positive n returns n - 1 pieces plus the remainder, unless tokens_only is TRUE. An empty string is handled before the n limit is checked. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive.
origin.value: A list of character vectors, or a character matrix when simplify is not FALSE.
origin.example:
result <- stri_split_regex("a,b,c", ",")[[1]]
cat(paste0('stri_split_regex("a,b,c", ",") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Split each string where a regular expression matches.
translation.usage: stri_split_regex(str, pattern, n=-1, omit_empty=False, tokens_only=False, simplify=False, opts_regex=None, **kwargs)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Regular expression, missing value, or list of those. An empty pattern yields NA.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Maximum number of pieces. Negative means every piece. A value at least 2147483646 is an error.

arguments.name: omit_empty
arguments.text: True drops empty pieces. NA replaces them with NA. False keeps them.

arguments.name: tokens_only
arguments.text: If true, a positive n keeps at most n whole pieces and drops the remainder.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: False returns a list. True pads a character matrix with empty strings. NA pads with NA.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: None, or a dict of only the regex settings that were supplied.

translation.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. A positive n returns n - 1 pieces plus the remainder, unless tokens_only is true. An empty string is handled before the n limit is checked. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive.
translation.value: A list of lists of strings, or a list of rows when simplify is not false.
translation.example:
from stringi.regex import stri_split_regex
result = stri_split_regex("a,b,c", ",")[0]
print('stri_split_regex("a,b,c", ",") returns ' + ', '.join(result) + '.')
